title: Personalized Bedding: Pick the Type, Size and Set
meta_description: Personalized bedding from $24.90 to $154.90. Compare fleece and sherpa blankets, duvet covers, quilts and comforters, plus sizes and pillowcase sets.
body_html:
Personalized bedding at Jeminise runs from $24.90 for a small fleece blanket to $154.90. What you should buy depends on three things: whether it's going on a sofa or a bed, the size it has to cover, and whether you want matching pillowcases.

In this guide

  1. What's in the Family Bedding range?
  2. Blanket, duvet cover, quilt or comforter: which one do you need?
  3. What size personalized blanket or bedding should you order?
  4. Do you need pillowcases with it?
  5. What can you personalize, and what should you have ready?
  6. Fleece or sherpa, and can you machine wash it?
  7. Worked example: an anniversary blanket for a shared sofa

What's in the Family Bedding range?

The range has 16 products. The six featured in this guide are all designed for two people: couple photos, hearts, a calendar layout and a deer couple motif. If you're shopping for one person or a whole household, keep that in mind as you browse.

What the range has in common:

  • 16 products, priced from $24.90 to $154.90
  • Five types: fleece blanket, sherpa blanket, duvet cover, quilt, comforter
  • Two text fields for personalization, stated on 14 of the 16 product pages
  • Machine washable, stated on 15 of the 16 product pages
  • Indoor and outdoor use in all seasons, stated on 14 of the 16 product pages

Some of those statements cover most of the range but not all of it, so read the page for the product you pick. The two text fields are a good example. Two products don't mention them, so confirm the fields are there before you write your text.

To narrow it down, start with the room. Is the piece going on a bed, or on a sofa or a lap? That one answer removes about half of the 16 options, and the next section shows which half.

You can see all 16 personalized designs side by side before deciding, but the type decision below will make that faster.

What to check

  • Is the piece for a bed or for a sofa?
  • Is the design made for a couple, or will it work for the person you're buying for?
  • Does the product page list two text fields?
  • Does the product page say machine washable?

Blanket, duvet cover, quilt or comforter: which one do you need?

This is the biggest decision, because it sets both the starting price and what else you might need. A blanket is a throw and doesn't have to fit a mattress. A duvet cover is a case that normally goes over a separate insert. Quilts and comforters are top layers for a bed.

To apply this at home, look at the bed you're buying for. If it already has a duvet insert, a duvet cover is the cheapest way to put the design on the whole bed. The product facts don't say whether an insert comes with the cover, so read the product page before you count on one. If you don't have an insert, compare a quilt or a comforter, or skip the bed and choose a blanket.

Not every design comes in every type. The couple photo design starts at $34.90 for bed pieces, and its product page lists the types it comes in.

What to check

  • Is there a duvet insert already, and does it match the bed size?
  • Does the starting price for your type fit your budget once you've picked the size?
  • Does the product page say what's included besides the cover or blanket?
  • Is the design you like offered in the type you need?

What size personalized blanket or bedding should you order?

The range uses two kinds of size: throw sizes for blankets, and bed sizes for bedding.

Throw sizes: 40" x 30" · 50" x 40" · 60" x 50" · 80" x 60" · Throw (60" x 70")

Bed sizes: US Twin (68" x 88") · US Full (78" x 88") · US Queen (88" x 88") · US King (104" x 88") · Twin (68" x 86") · Full (80" x 90") · Queen (90" x 90")

Starting prices by size, where given:

  • 40" x 30": from $24.90
  • 50" x 40": from $34.90
  • 60" x 50": from $44.90
  • US Twin (68" x 88"): from $34.90

There are two Twin, Full and Queen sizes with slightly different measurements. Each product page shows only the sizes that product comes in, so compare your measurements with the list on the page you're ordering from, not with the full list above.

How to measure. For a bed, measure the top of the mattress across and from head to foot, and write down its depth. A duvet cover should match your insert, not the mattress. For a quilt or comforter, choose a size wider than the mattress if you want it to hang over the sides. For a sofa throw, measure the seat width and the height of the person who'll use it most. A 40" x 30" piece covers a lap, not a whole adult.

The photo and heart design is also made for the bed, starting at $34.90, so it's a good one to measure against.

What to check

  • Mattress width, length and depth, written down before you order
  • If it's a duvet cover, the size printed on your insert's label
  • Which size list your chosen product uses
  • Whether the sofa throw is long enough for the tallest person using it

Do you need pillowcases with it?

Bedding comes with five set options:

  • No pillowcases
  • 1 pillowcase (20" x 30")
  • 2 pillowcases (20" x 30")
  • 2 pillowcases + 1 sheet
  • 4 pillowcases (20" x 30")

The lowest starting price without pillowcases is $34.90, and the lowest with one pillowcase is $44.90. Those two figures may come from different sizes or types, so they don't tell you exactly what a pillowcase adds to your order. Check the price change on the product page as you switch options.

To apply this, count the pillows on the bed and measure one. Every pillowcase in the range is listed as 20" x 30". If your pillows are much bigger, the matching set may not fit them, and "No pillowcases" is the safer choice. A couple usually needs two. The four-pillowcase option suits a bed with a second row of pillows.

Only one option includes a sheet. The product facts don't give its size or say whether it's fitted or flat, so check that on the product page if the sheet is the reason you're choosing the set. For a bed set with a different look, the deer couple heart design starts at $34.90.

What to check

  • How many pillows are on the bed
  • Whether your pillows are close to 20" x 30"
  • Whether you need a sheet, and what type the set includes
  • The price difference shown when you switch set options on your chosen product

What can you personalize, and what should you have ready?

On 14 of the 16 product pages, personalization is described as two text fields. Most couples use them for two names, or for a name and a date. Several designs are also built around a photo.

A portrait design like the one above depends on the photo more than anything else. A sharp, evenly lit picture with both faces clear gives the print the most to work with. Hearts designs do the same with a smaller photo.

The photo hearts blanket starts at $24.90, which makes it one of the lowest-priced photo options in the range.

The product facts don't say how many photos each design takes, what resolution it needs, or whether you see a proof before printing. The product page is the place to check all three. Write your two lines and choose your photo before you open it, so you can enter them straight away.

What to check

  • Your two lines of text, with names spelled exactly as they should print
  • Any date written in the format you want to see
  • A sharp, well-lit photo with both faces clearly visible, if the design uses one
  • Whether the product page shows a preview before you add it to the cart

Fleece or sherpa, and can you machine wash it?

The blankets come in two materials, and the starting prices are different:

  • Fleece: from $24.90
  • Sherpa: from $39.90

On 13 of the 16 product pages, the fabric is described as "Sherpa and Fleece fabric with two polyester layers." That description doesn't say which side faces up or how the two options differ beyond their names, so compare the photos on the product page if the feel matters to you.

Choose based on budget and use. If the blanket is a gift to fold over a sofa and you want to stay near the bottom of the price range, start with fleece. If you'd rather have sherpa, budget from $39.90 and compare the same size in both materials on the product page.

Machine washable is stated on 15 of the 16 product pages. Wash temperature and drying settings aren't part of that statement, so follow the care label once it arrives. Fourteen pages also say the blanket works indoors and outdoors in all seasons. That's useful if it'll go to picnics or live in the car as well as on the sofa.

If you want a less sentimental design, the neon skeleton hands heart blanket starts at $24.90.

What to check

  • The price of your size in fleece compared with sherpa
  • That your chosen product page says machine washable
  • The care label for wash and dry settings
  • Whether it'll be used outdoors, where washing will matter more often

Worked example: an anniversary blanket for a shared sofa

This is a made-up case to show the decision step by step. It isn't a customer story.

Sam wants an anniversary gift for a partner and wants to spend less than the cheapest comforter, which starts at $64.90. The couple watches films on a three-seat sofa, and they already have bedding they like. Sam wants both their names and the wedding date on it, plus a photo.

Step 1: Type. The gift is for the sofa, so it's a blanket. The duvet cover, quilt and comforter are out.

Step 2: Material. Fleece starts at $24.90 and sherpa at $39.90. Both fit the limit, but starting with fleece leaves more room for a larger size. Sam starts with fleece.

Step 3: Size. Two people sharing a sofa need more than a lap throw. The 50" x 40" starts at $34.90 and the 60" x 50" at $44.90. Sam picks 60" x 50", because both people fit under it and its starting price is still below the comforter's.

Step 4: Design. Sam wants a date and a photo, so the calendar blanket that marks your date beside a photo fits. One text field takes "Sam & Alex" and the other takes the wedding date.

Step 5: Check. Before ordering, Sam confirms on that product page that the 60" x 50" fleece price is still within the limit. If it isn't, the fallback is 50" x 40" in fleece.

If your case needs a bed piece instead, use the same steps. Take the type from the table, the size from your mattress or insert, and the set option from your pillow count. Once you know the type and size, narrow the Family Bedding range to designs that fit.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much does personalized bedding from Jeminise cost?

The Family Bedding range has 16 products priced from $24.90 to $154.90. Fleece blankets start at $24.90, duvet covers at $34.90, sherpa blankets at $39.90, quilts at $46.90 and comforters at $64.90. The final price depends on the size and set option you choose.

What can I personalize on Jeminise bedding?

Most products in the range, 14 of 16, offer two text fields. They're often used for two names, or a name and a date. Several designs also include a photo of the couple.

Is Jeminise personalized bedding machine washable?

Machine washable is stated on 15 of the 16 product pages in the Family Bedding range. Check the page for the specific product you're buying, and follow the care label for wash and dry settings.

What sizes does personalized bedding come in?

Blankets come in 40" x 30", 50" x 40", 60" x 50", 80" x 60" and Throw (60" x 70"). Bed sizes include US Twin (68" x 88"), US Full (78" x 88"), US Queen (88" x 88") and US King (104" x 88"), plus Twin (68" x 86"), Full (80" x 90") and Queen (90" x 90"). Each product page lists the sizes that product comes in.

Can I get matching pillowcases?

Yes. Set options are no pillowcases, 1 pillowcase, 2 pillowcases, 2 pillowcases with 1 sheet, or 4 pillowcases. Every pillowcase is listed as 20" x 30".
